questions.q: What is the correct action for a normal outstanding check that was issued only a few days ago?
options: Immediately escalate it to the bank as an error
Reverse it in Payables right away
Usually nothing yet — wait for the bank to process it on a future statement
Force a manual match against an unrelated transaction
questions.explain: A recently outstanding check is a normal timing difference; it simply hasn't been cashed yet, and typically needs no action beyond waiting.

questions.q: What is the correct resolution when a bank statement line has no system counterpart because the transaction was never entered into Oracle?
options: Record the missing transaction in the appropriate subledger
Delete the statement line
Escalate it to the bank as an error
Apply an account-level tolerance rule to ignore it
questions.explain: A missing transaction should be recorded (or confirmed as pending entry), not forced into a match against something that doesn't exist.

questions.q: Who must resolve a genuine bank error, such as a wrong amount charged to an account?
options: The bank itself, via direct escalation; Cash Management cannot fix it from inside Oracle
Cash Management can silently correct it without involving the bank
Receivables, by reversing an unrelated receipt
No one — bank errors self-correct automatically
questions.explain: A bank-side error requires contacting the bank directly; Cash Management can document the discrepancy but cannot fix the bank's own error.

questions.q: Why do most implementations 'age' unreconciled items by days outstanding?
options: To automatically delete items older than a set number of days
To distinguish normal timing differences from items likely to be real problems needing attention
Because Oracle requires aging before a statement can be loaded
To calculate interest earned on the bank account
questions.explain: Aging helps separate normal timing noise from items old enough to likely represent a missing transaction, bank error, or mistake needing attention.

questions.q: In the worked example, how was the 11-day-old $600 item ultimately resolved?
options: Escalated to the bank as an error
Left unreconciled indefinitely
Identified as a duplicate entry and corrected at the source in Receivables
Matched using a one-to-many rule
questions.explain: The $600 item was a duplicate entry made by an AR clerk, and the fix was to correct it at the source rather than work around it in reconciliation.
